metaData.originalTitle: Harness Engineering 落地前，先想清楚这几个问题
metaData.title: Think Through These Issues Before Implementing Harness Engineering
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the practice of Tencent's Dola data analysis product, this article systematically elaborates on two key tasks for frontend developers in the AI era: optimizing AI product experience through a three-dimensional scoring recommendation engine and a self-developed code highlighting component, and adapting to AI Coding through engineering constraint refactoring and programming paradigm reflection.
metaData.summary: This is an in-depth technical practice article from the Tencent Cloud Developer official account. Author franslee, based on the practical experience of his team's AI data analysis assistant Dola, systematically explores two core propositions for frontend development in the AI era. The first part focuses on "Serving AI Products Well," detailing how a three-dimensional scoring recommendation engine combining data features, SQL features, and user prompts improved chart recommendation accuracy from 55% to nearly 90%. It also covers the self-developed Code Highlighting Component 3.0 based on the CSS Custom Highlight API and multi-threaded architecture, solving pain points like selection loss during streaming dialogue, DOM explosion, and Ctrl+F unavailability. The second part focuses on "Serving AI Coding Well," proposing a Harness Engineering approach that advocates transforming legacy projects to be more suitable for AI collaboration by establishing machine-readable engineering rules, converging code exports, and extracting Design Tokens. The article also deeply reflects on how, in an era where AI-generated code is becoming mainstream, programming paradigms should shift from "elegant and concise" to "explicit, searchable, straightforward, and moderately repetitive." It points out that the role of frontend developers is transitioning from "syntax craftsmen" to "intention decomposers and architecture decision-makers."

mainPoints.point: In AI data analysis scenarios, chart recommendations should combine data features, SQL features, and user prompts in a three-dimensional scoring system, rather than relying solely on data features.
mainPoints.explanation: Traditional chart recommendation libraries only recommend based on field types and distributions, resulting in low accuracy in AI dialogue scenarios. The author's proposed three-dimensional scoring engine leverages structural information from SQL like GROUP BY and ORDER BY, along with intent keywords from user prompts, boosting recommendation accuracy from 55% to nearly 90%.

mainPoints.point: The core conflict in streaming code highlighting is the architectural mismatch between the DOM model of traditional highlighting libraries and the AI dialogue scenario.
mainPoints.explanation: Traditional highlighting libraries rebuild the DOM tree on every render, causing selection loss and DOM explosion during streaming output. The author uses the CSS Custom Highlight API for coloring based on a single textNode, combined with multi-threaded tokenization and rAF throttling, solving issues like preserving streaming selections, enabling Ctrl+F search, and maintaining performance in long sessions.

mainPoints.point: The core of adapting legacy projects for AI Coding is making engineering rules machine-readable, rather than relying solely on more powerful models.
mainPoints.explanation: AI can only take an 'average' approach in inconsistent historical code. By establishing structured rule files (.mdc) in the repository, automatically distributing them to directories recognized by AI tools, and converging code exports and Design Tokens, the variance in AI output can be significantly reduced, building team trust in AI Coding.

mainPoints.point: In the AI Coding era, programming paradigms should shift from 'elegant and concise' to 'explicit, searchable, straightforward, and moderately repetitive.'
mainPoints.explanation: When AI can generate code quickly, 'typing less' is no longer scarce. What is truly scarce is code understandability, searchability, and local modifiability. Past practices that sacrificed readability to reduce typing costs—such as Sass nested concatenation, excessive destructuring, and flashy type gymnastics—need to be re-evaluated.

mainPoints.point: The role of frontend developers is transitioning from 'syntax craftsmen' to 'intention decomposers and architecture decision-makers.'
mainPoints.explanation: In the future, the core competency of frontend developers will no longer be the speed of writing code by hand, but the ability to accurately decompose problems, define boundaries, judge the rationality of AI-generated solutions, and design maintainable architectures—shifting from 'how to write' to 'what to do.'

keyQuotes: The core of adapting legacy projects for AI Coding is not adding a plugin or writing a few prompts, but transforming the project into a form that AI can easily write correctly.
In the AI Coding era, code must not only be human-friendly but also AI-friendly.
What truly needs reflection is: have we sacrificed readability, searchability, and modifiability for the sake of writing pleasure?
Frontend developers will gradually transition from 'syntax craftsmen' to intention decomposers, architecture decision-makers, and AI code reviewers.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: From Toy to Productivity: Demystifying AI Agent Harness Engineering Through Real Projects
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the practical experience of the real-world project Aegis, this article systematically elaborates on the concept, architectural boundaries, and implementation methods of Harness Engineering. It argues that in enterprise engineering environments, constraining and governing non-deterministic large models by building a control plane is the key to transforming AI Agents from toys into productive tools, and it drives the migration of the engineer's role from code executor to goal controller.

relatedArticles.title: Reflections on the Paradigm Shift in AI Software Engineering
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically argues from an engineering philosophy perspective that software engineering has never truly been engineered, and that large language models, as cognitive engines, fill this critical gap, proposing a complete paradigm shift from human-centered to AI-centered, closed-loop-first, and divide-and-conquer inheritance.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: RAG is Dead? No, Grep is Back!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the leaked source code of Claude Code, this article deeply deconstructs its abandonment of RAG and vector retrieval in favor of an LLM-driven multi-round iterative Grep search mechanism. It compares this approach with Cursor and Codex, demonstrating the feasibility and design philosophy of a zero-index solution in code search scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: Thinking About Agentic Engineering from First Principles
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically derives six core best practices for Agentic Engineering from first principles and introduces a modular, Skill-based open-source framework, aiming to combine engineering discipline with AI capabilities to reliably improve software engineering quality under complex constraints.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.
